title: Fodhelper spawns a suspicious child process
description: Detects fodhelper.exe spawning a command interpreter or administrative utility associated with UAC bypass activity.

hypothesis.summary: An adversary may abuse the auto-elevated Fodhelper binary to launch a high-integrity command interpreter or proxy-execution utility without a normal consent prompt.
hypothesis.rationale: MITRE documents Fodhelper abuse under UAC bypass and SigmaHQ maintains a matching parent-child analytic; rare legitimate automation can still create the same process relationship.
hypothesis.detection_goal: Identify selected command interpreters and administrative utilities spawned directly by Fodhelper while leaving ordinary Fodhelper children, other parents and adjacent auto-elevated binaries unmatched.

data_sources.name: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint process events

triage.summary: Determine why Fodhelper launched the selected child and correlate registry changes, integrity level and subsequent commands before treating it as a UAC bypass.
steps: Review the child command, account, process tree, integrity level and endpoint role.
Inspect recent per-user registry changes associated with the ms-settings handler and correlate follow-on execution, persistence and network activity.
Confirm an approved management or testing workflow; contain the endpoint and remove unauthorized handler changes when unexplained.
false_positives: Approved administrative automation or security testing that intentionally launches a selected child through Fodhelper

validation.expected_outcome: Match selected suspicious children spawned by Fodhelper; do not match ordinary children, another parent, another auto-elevated binary or missing parent context.
